source_snapshot.test_name_items: Fan speed change test with power assume.
source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check system would chnage fan speed in different power consumption.
1. Boot into OS.
2.Run BurnIN test to add system power consumption
3. Check fan speed change with different stress test and power consumption.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure fan speed would change with different power consumption.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands:
# agent host: sample fan RPM now, apply a brief CPU load on the DUT, then re-sample
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'fan'
---load (DUT, 30s)---
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "sudo stress-ng --cpu $(nproc) --timeout 30s 2>&1 & sleep 40"
---after (agent host)---
ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" sdr list 2>&1 | grep -iE 'fan'

original_test_intent: Verify automatic fan control changes RPM appropriately across approved BurnIN workload or power-consumption levels.
original_method: Boot the SUT into the approved OS, run the named/project-approved BurnIN profiles that create distinct measured power states, continuously record power, fan RPM and temperatures through settle/cooldown, and compare fan response with the platform control specification.
manual_activity: The owner selects the platform, BurnIN profiles, duration, power metric and expected response. The approved workload, synchronized telemetry, comparisons and cleanup can then run automatically; engineer verdict remains separate.
required_inputs: Approved BurnIN tool/version/license and workload dimensions
At least two defined power/load levels, duration/dwell and actual power measurement or accepted proxy
Expected fan RPM/zone response, hysteresis/settling tolerance and automatic-control baseline
Thermal/power/fan abort limits, maintenance window, OOB recovery and one-user approval
safety_requirements: Do not replace BurnIN with stress-ng or guess a 30-second duration without project approval.
Confirm automatic fan control, workload scope and cleanup before starting.
Continuously monitor power, temperatures, fan RPM, alarms, host and OOB health; abort and cool down on any limit.
Preserve all telemetry/logs and the first failure; no automatic restart or retry.
agent_execution_scope: Validate and launch each approved BurnIN profile and record its exact parameters/status.
Collect synchronized power/load, per-zone fan RPM, temperature, throttle/alarm and BMC/host telemetry.
Apply the supplied response/hysteresis rules, stop/clean up workload and report comparisons without issuing PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Define/approve the load-power matrix, response criteria and safety limits.
Provide the package and project-specific power measurement method.
Review evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Not equivalent. A 30-second CPU-only stress-ng run neither preserves the named BurnIN method nor establishes distinct power profiles, settling behavior or full-system coverage; pre/post grep snapshots can miss transient response.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the reviewed source-linked project script and owner-approved BurnIN interface with continuous telemetry. Retain stress-ng only if explicitly approved as a documented project override with its reduced coverage.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BurnIN, different stress/power levels and both one-minute library fields are retained; the source does not state a workload duration, so none is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a versioned multi-level load matrix while sampling actual platform power, each fan zone and temperatures at a fixed interval through baseline, ramp, steady state and cooldown.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The SUT and fan-control firmware for which the response curve is supplied.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BurnIN, OS, BIOS, BMC/CPLD and monitoring-tool versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Source-linked project script, approved BurnIN documentation and platform fan-control specification.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds quantitative power, time-series sampling and hysteresis-aware evaluation without changing the workload intent.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves different-power response; a CPU-only shortcut is not equivalent unless expressly scoped.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Load levels, power metric, response curve, settle/cooldown and limits.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Power and fan response can lag and depend on inlet temperature; single snapshots are insufficient.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve different tools, load levels or duration, but the report must identify executed profiles and cannot claim source BurnIN or unexecuted power ranges. Parameter selection does not reduce full automation capability.
expected_evidence: Platform/firmware/tool identity, load-power matrix, response/hysteresis criteria and approval
Exact workload commands/configuration and exit status per profile
Time-aligned power/load, per-fan RPM, temperatures, thresholds and alarms through cooldown
Process cleanup, automatic-control/final-health verification and unexpected logs

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion consistently require fan-speed change across different power consumption. Missing quantitative profiles and thresholds are readiness inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The tool, matrix, duration and expected curve can be provided per project. The test remains fully automatable once those inputs are approved.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Reject the unapproved short CPU-only substitution and sparse sampling.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retain V2's defined profiles, power evidence, continuous monitoring and cleanup; reclassify to FULLY AUTOMATABLE because no manual core is stated.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates missing project test parameters from capability and preserves explicit coverage accounting.

review_improvement: Turns an undefined load notion into a project-supplied quantitative response plan without inventing a universal workload or fan curve.
independent_technical_reasoning: Both stimulus and acceptance evidence are software-controllable and machine-readable once a load plan and response curve exist. The requirement for owner-supplied parameters and approval is execution readiness, not human core activity, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE follows the locked rule.
